jobs.title: Senior Responsible Supply Chain Manager, Western Hemisphere
jobs.description:
who we are
lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

about this team
The Responsible Supply Chain team works to support the wellbeing of the people who make lululemon products, and supports supply chain resilience, manage risk and social compliance, and build brand purpose. We monitor working conditions in all facilities producing for lululemon, though our internal team and together with external partners. We work together with cross-functional partners within lululemon to support responsible practices of doing business in our everyday operations. We collaborate with our vendors, and external stakeholders to foster resilience in the garment industry and build better systems.

core responsibilities
Lead social responsible supply chain works of Western Hemisphere region through strategic planning, implementation and partnership with key stakeholders to foster supply chain resilience and well-being of people in the supply chain.
- Manages vendor RSC performance for the region, including timely assessments & effective and sustainable remediation.
- Leads regional engagement with relevant stakeholders, including vendors, workers, industry organizations, Civil Society Organizations.
- Provides regular updates about regional risk and landscape trends, as well as vendor performance against RSC objectives and KPIs.
- Engages with internal cross-functional partners around vendor RSC performance & improvement work.
- Supports regional implementation of globally developed implementation & engagement programs to support lululemon’s commitment towards the people who make our product.
- Provides consistent and accurate data, analytics and reporting.
- Manages a team of regional assessors, 3rd party consultants, and implementation partners.

qualifications
- 10+ years’ experience in Responsible Supply Chain, Ethical Trade, Sustainability, Human Rights in region, leading monitoring & improvement programs.
- 7+ years leading Social Compliance assessments on-site, as well as remediation work with individual factories and regions.
- 5+ years of people leadership and management.
- Exceptional understanding of regional risks and Human Rights and sustainability landscape.
- Strong cross- cultural communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in written and spoken English; fluency in Spanish is preferred.
- Program/project management and delivery or equivalent consulting experience.
- Strong relationship management skills & capabilities with vendors, regional stakeholders (e.g. industry organizations, peer brands, workers’ rights groups and civil society organizations)
- Seasoned team leader and passionate human rights and sustainable business advocate, exceptional integrity and independent working

must haves
- Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
- Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
- Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
- Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
- Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
- Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.

additional notes
Authorization to work in Canada is required for this role.

compensation and benefits package
lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from $141,400 - $185,600 CAD annually;  the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program and, subject to program eligibility requirements.

As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive, and growth-focused environment for our people.

about this team:
The Global Procurement team are trusted business advisors who strategically partner with internal stakeholders and external suppliers to create value and mitigate risk in strategic non-product purchases for the global organization. The team supports the business in increasing its profitability and return on investment by creating value in our indirect supply chain through strategic & stakeholder-centric procurement. From providing category expertise, market insights, cost savings opportunities, supplier performance and relationship management & developing short and long-term strategies, the Global Procurement team plays a key role in value delivery for our business.

Rooted within Global Procurement is the Global Procurement Strategy & Analytics function. This team enables value delivery across Category Management through Procurement Enablement, Procurement Intelligence, and Responsible Procurement. Beyond establishing strong data and process foundations, the team also drives alignment to lululemon’s core values and mandates related to People and Planet.

a day in the life:
Reporting to the Director, Procurement – Strategy & Analytics, the Senior Manager, Responsible Procurement plays a critical role in embedding lululemon’s values across our supplier ecosystem. In close partnership with Legal, Risk & Advisory, Cybersecurity, and Business Units, this role leads the Responsible Procurement function, shaping and advancing supplier risk, performance, relationship, and impact strategies and programs across Global Procurement.

what you’ll do:
- Set and lead the Responsible Procurement strategy across Global Procurement, defining priorities, roadmaps, and measurable outcomes aligned to lululemon’s enterprise goals
- Oversee the design and scaling of global programs, ensuring that their frameworks are integrated, consistent, and embedded across all categories and regions
- Drive enterprise-wide adoption of Responsible Procurement practices, embedding requirements into sourcing, contracting, category planning, and supplier management processes
- Establish governance, operating rhythms, and decision forums, enabling cross-functional alignment with Legal, Risk & Advisory, Cybersecurity, IDEA, and Business stakeholders
- Own program performance and value delivery, defining KPIs, monitoring outcomes, and driving continuous improvement across adoption, compliance, risk mitigation, and supplier impact
- Guide category teams in translating strategy into action, ensuring supplier strategies reflect risk, performance, inclusion, and sustainability considerations
- Lead senior stakeholder engagement, influencing Directors and above to integrate Responsible Procurement into business priorities and decision-making
- Oversee insights, reporting, and analytics, ensuring data-driven decision-making through clear dashboards, actionable insights, and continuous feedback loops
- Identify and advance external partnerships, including supplier councils, certifying bodies, and third-party providers to strengthen program reach and effectiveness
- Champion change and capability building, driving awareness, education, and mindset shifts to enable a culture of responsible, value-driven procurement

qualifications:
- Required: Bachelor’s degree
- Preferred: MBA, SCMP, PMP or other relevant professional designation or certification
- 7+ years Third-party Risk Management, Supplier Relationship Management programs, ESG applied to indirect Procurement and/or Procurement Strategy
- 3+ years of indirect procurement category experience
- Proficiency Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint).
- Experience using AI to unlock efficiency and P2P/e-sourcing platform knowledge is an asset
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Core capabilities:
- Responsible Procurement: Ensures strategic sourcing integrates supplier risk, inclusion, sustainability and performance considerations.
- Relationship Management: Builds essential trust with the stakeholder base. Is able to handle complex multi-customer issues that involve a number of areas. Sets expectations and tone for organization’s stakeholder engagement strategy and operations.
- Change Management & Evolution: Understands and recognizes opportunities for change and creates strategies. Leads organization through preparation and execution. Is at the forefront of aligning change with organizational impact. Provides direction on appropriate change to enable business objectives and ensures consistent application across all initiatives and stakeholder interactions.
- Communication: Understands multiple methods and styles of communication. Manages communication style according to the audience and to ensure maximum effectiveness. Able to adjust style intuitively to meet needs at hand.
- Market Awareness: Knowledge of the vendor landscape and industry trends.
- Ownership: Has the ability to handle complex issues. Takes ownership of issues and sees them through resolution while providing guidance and support to other team members.
- Facilitation Skills: Advanced skills in facilitation and storytelling. Ensures business review meetings are facilitated with strength, conviction and from a place of collaboration and action across tier 1 and 2 suppliers.
- Decision Making: Strategic decision-maker for the organization. Actively seeks and applies the input of others and seeks broad consultation. Demonstrates good judgment and communicates basis for decisions in a way that makes sense for the organization and all levels of stakeholders. Makes policy decisions within scope of organization’s goals and values
- Supplier Risk: Has the ability to develop organizational third-party risk management strategies and lead initiatives. Is involved in leadership risk mitigation discussions with key suppliers.
- Supplier Performance: Creates an internal environment that holds the supply base accountable to assist the organization in meeting its objectives and drives initiatives that improve performance, efficiency, cost, quality and value. Serves as escalation contact for major issues with supplier performance
- ESG: Fully understands and internally/externally advocates regulations with respect to ESG responsibilities, policies and procedures applied to indirect procurement. Able to design approaches for incorporating these objectives for business benefit.

They are responsible for writing the store’s weekly schedule, leading the floor and ensuring a high quality guest experience, and  people-related actions (including completing payroll, approving time off, and other documentation).

Core Responsibilities of the Job
- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations strategy and vision for the store and cascade to team members using your independent judgment.
- Plan, prepare, and manage team member schedules, taking into account labor requirements, availability, safety requirements, inventory deliveries, and budget considerations to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of operations.
- Manage the budget and analyze other business data and metrics (e.g., P&L statement, expenses) to inform planning processes (e.g., quarterly business review and sales planning) and drive results.
- Monitor progress against financial goals (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly) to evaluate sales and collect information to support with strategy, including – for outlet stores – to inform pricing targets.
- Sustain operational excellence by ensuring inventory accuracy and verifying labor is scheduled to efficiently execute product operations.
- Oversee and monitor execution of market-relevant omnichannel programs (e.g., buy online/pickup in store and ship from store options) according to company standards.
- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives.

- Perform people-related actions to update team member personnel information, including completing payroll, approving time off requests, approving shift swaps, and executing job changes/transfers accurately and within required timeframes.

- Inform other store leaders of projected team growth needs to support the building of a strong and diverse team based on operational trends and results.
- Actively monitor product levels and organize accurate, efficient inventory receiving and processing to sustain operational excellence.

Eligibility

Assistant Managers, Operations manage business enablers (including financial, profit and loss [P&L], budget, expenses, and cash) and ensure inventory, supplies, vendor relationships, technology, and facilities are maintained and maximized. They are responsible for writing the store’s weekly schedule and accomplishing people-related administrative activities (including completing payroll and other documentation). Assistant Managers, Operations also execute company-driven operations-focused projects and initiatives at the store level.

Core Responsibilities of the Job

Operations, Product, and Strategy
- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations vision for the store and cascade to team members.
- Plan and prepare weekly team member schedule according to labor requirements, availability, and budget considerations.
- Move dynamically on the retail floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team, and guests.
- Review, monitor, and partner with Store Manager to manage the budget and other business data and metrics (e.g., P&L statement, expenses) and inform planning processes (e.g., quarterly business review and sales planning).
- Provide retail floor leadership to team members, including planning retail floor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of retail floor operations.
- Support sell-through management by ensuring accuracy of inventory counts and coordinating labor hours to efficiently receive product deliveries.
- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives (e.g., from the SSC).
- Understand and adhere to people safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe work environment.
- Perform work in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and laws or regulations.

Leadership and People
- Create and foster a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and celebrating differences to ensure a supportive, productive, and fun experience for all team members.
- Perform administrative actions to support team members, including completing payroll, approving vacation and time off requests, approving shift swaps, and other documentation according to policies and procedures.
- Inform people managers of projected team growth needs to support the building of a strong and diverse team based on operational trends and results.
- Establish supportive and productive relationships with all team members, focusing on personal and professional development.

Guest Experience and Community
- Facilitate a seamless end-to-end guest experience by monitoring the incorporation of omnichannel programs (e.g., in-store guest transactions, buy online pickup in store, phone sales, and ship from store).
- Collaborate with team members to ensure an optimal guest experience that values guests’ time and supports store operations.
- Resolve guest feedback and address issues, including guest escalations and urgent requests, helping to “make it right” for guests.

Budget Responsibility
- Accountable for delegated aspects of controllable budget and labor hours

People Management
- Leadership role indirectly responsible for subset of store employees as delegated by Store Manager

- Inclusion & Diversity:  Creates/supports an inclusive environment that values/celebrates differences
- Integrity: Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner

- Leadership: Is able and desires to lead and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work
- Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve common goals; seeks connections, partnerships, and diverse perspectives
- Decision Making/Problem Solving: Identifies opportunities for improvement; evaluates alternatives and makes effective, timely decisions
- Strategic Thinking:  Considers the lasting implications of decisions; sets a plan and makes decisions aligned with company strategy, vision, and values
- Business Acumen: Is able to quickly understand and address business information (e.g., profit and loss statements, budgets and sales forecasts, retail strategy and approaches)
- Interactive Communication:  Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others

Job Requirements

Eligibility
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located
- Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods

Schedule/Availability
- Work occurs on a variable schedule which could include early mornings, mornings, afternoons, evenings, late nights or overnights as well as weekends and holidays

Experience
- 1 year experience managing business operations and administration, including experience with scheduling and management of designated labor hours and managing projects or processes

Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)
- Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
- Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
- Experience: 1 year retail or sales specific management experience

Work Context (e.g., environment, interactions, physical)
- Work occurs in an environment with bright lights and loud music
- Work is accomplished as part of a team and also independently
- Work may involve managing conflict or mediating problems between others or deescalating guest issues
- Work involves reaching out to meet and build relationships with strangers/new people, and to strengthen existing community partnerships
- Work is sometimes conducted on a computer or other technical devices, including to meet with others virtually
- Work involves moving through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work, but can also involve sitting for extended periods of time (i.e., more than 1 hour)
- Work may occasionally involve moving boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg)

Compensation & Benefits Package

Base Pay Range:  $27.00-$36.50 subject to minimum wage in the location
Target Bonus: 25%
Total Target Base Pay Range : $33.75 - $45.63/hour

- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations vision for the store and cascade to team members.

- Provide retail floor leadership to team members, including planning retail floor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of retail floor operations.

- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives (e.g., from the SSC).

- Business Acumen: Is able to quickly understand and address business information (e.g., profit and loss statements, budgets and sales forecasts, retail strategy and approaches)
- Interactive Communication:  Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others

Job Requirements

Eligibility
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located
- Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods

Schedule/Availability
- Work occurs on a variable schedule which could include early mornings, mornings, afternoons, evenings, late nights or overnights as well as weekends and holidays

Experience
- 1 year experience managing business operations and administration, including experience with scheduling and management of designated labor hours and managing projects or processes

Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)
- Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
- Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
- Experience: 1 year retail or sales specific management experience

- Work occurs in an environment with bright lights and loud music
- Work is accomplished as part of a team and also independently
- Work may involve managing conflict or mediating problems between others or deescalating guest issues
- Work involves reaching out to meet and build relationships with strangers/new people, and to strengthen existing community partnerships
- Work is sometimes conducted on a computer or other technical devices, including to meet with others virtually
- Work involves moving through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work, but can also involve sitting for extended periods of time (i.e., more than 1 hour)

Nous devons notre succès à nos produits innovants, à l’importance que nous accordons à nos magasins, à notre engagement envers notre personnel et aux connexions incroyables que nous établissons dans chaque communauté où nous nous trouvons. En tant qu’entreprise, nous nous efforçons de créer un changement positif pour construire un avenir sain et prospère. Cela consiste notamment à créer un environnement équitable, inclusif et axé sur la croissance de nos employés.

Résumé du poste

Le gérant adjoint responsable du fonctionnement joue un rôle primordial dans l’équipe de gestion du magasin : il s’assure que les activités à notre magasin de vente au détail se déroulent sans problème et qu’elles obtiennent du succès. Le gérant adjoint responsable du fonctionnement gère les aspects facilitant l’activité commerciale (notamment l’aspect financier, les états des résultats, le budget, les dépenses et les caisses). De plus, il s’assure que les stocks, les fournitures, les relations avec les fournisseurs, la technologie et les installations sont maintenus et optimisés. Il doit mettre sur papier l’horaire hebdomadaire du magasin et effectuer des tâches administratives liées au personnel (notamment la préparation des fiches de paie et d’autres documents). Le gérant adjoint responsable du fonctionnement exécute aussi les projets et les initiatives de fonctionnement relevant de l’entreprise à l’échelle du magasin.

Principales responsabilités liées au poste

Activités, produits et stratégies
- Concrétiser la vision du gérant de magasin concernant le fonctionnement du magasin et la transmettre en cascade aux membres de l’équipe.
- Planifier et préparer les horaires hebdomadaires des membres de l’équipe en fonction des besoins en main-d’œuvre, de la disponibilité et des contraintes budgétaires.
- Se déplacer de manière dynamique dans le magasin pour évaluer les besoins de l’entreprise, de l’équipe et des invités et y répondre.
- Effectuer des examens, faire des suivis et collaborer avec le gérant de magasin pour gérer le budget et les autres données et mesures commerciales (p. ex., les états des résultats, les dépenses) et fournir des informations sur les processus de planification (p. ex., la révision trimestrielle des affaires du magasin et la planification des ventes).
- Fournir un encadrement de la surface de vente aux membres de l’équipe, notamment en planifiant la présence sur le plancher pour la vente au détail et en prenant des décisions pour maintenir l’efficacité et l’efficience des opérations de la surface de vente.
- Contribuer à la gestion par l’écoulement des stocks en assurant l’exactitude de l’inventaire et en coordonnant les heures de la main-d’œuvre pour une réception efficace des livraisons de produits.
- Exécuter les directives, les projets et les initiatives de fonctionnement à l’échelle de l’entreprise (p. ex., depuis le SSC; centre d’assistance aux magasins).
- Comprendre les politiques et procédures de sécurité du personnel et y adhérer afin de maintenir un environnement de travail sécuritaire.
- Effectuer le travail conformément aux politiques, procédures et lois ou règlements applicables.

Leadership et personnel
- Créer et favoriser un environnement d’équipe respectueux et inclusif en accueillant et en célébrant les différences afin de garantir une expérience favorable, productive et amusante pour tous les membres de l’équipe.
- Effectuer les démarches administratives nécessaires au soutien des membres de l’équipe, notamment en remplissant les fiches de paie, en approuvant les demandes de vacances et de congés, en approuvant les permutations de quart de travail et toute autre documentation conformément aux politiques et aux procédures.
- Informer les gestionnaires de personnel des besoins liés à la croissance de l’équipe et projetés afin de favoriser la consolidation d’une équipe forte et diversifiée en fonction des tendances d’exploitation et des résultats.
- Établir des relations soutenantes et productives avec les membres de l’équipe, en mettant l’accent sur le développement personnel et professionnel.

Expérience-invité et communication
- Favoriser une expérience-invité harmonieuse du début à la fin en surveillant l’intégration des programmes omnicanaux (p. ex., la surveillance des transactions avec les invités en magasin, l’achat en ligne et le ramassage en magasin, les ventes par téléphone et l’expédition à partir du magasin).
- Collaborer avec les membres de l’équipe afin de garantir une expérience-invité optimale qui valorise le temps des invités et favorise le fonctionnement du magasin.

jobs.title: Assistant Manager, Operations | Westboro
jobs.description:
Who We Are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

Job Summary

The Assistant Manager, Operations role is an essential part of the store leadership team and is responsible for making sure our retail business runs smoothly and successfully. Assistant Managers, Operations manage business enablers (including financial, profit and loss [P&L], budget, expenses, and cash) and ensure inventory, supplies, vendor relationships, technology, and facilities are maintained and maximized. They are responsible for writing the store’s weekly schedule and accomplishing people-related administrative activities (including completing payroll and other documentation). Assistant Managers, Operations also execute company-driven operations-focused projects and initiatives at the store level.

Core Responsibilities of the Job

Operations, Product, and Strategy
- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations vision for the store and cascade to team members.
- Plan and prepare weekly team member schedule according to labor requirements, availability, and budget considerations.
- Move dynamically on the retail floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team, and guests.
- Review, monitor, and partner with Store Manager to manage the budget and other business data and metrics (e.g., P&L statement, expenses) and inform planning processes (e.g., quarterly business review and sales planning).
- Provide retail floor leadership to team members, including planning retail floor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of retail floor operations.
- Support sell-through management by ensuring accuracy of inventory counts and coordinating labor hours to efficiently receive product deliveries.
- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives (e.g., from the SSC).
- Understand and adhere to people safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe work environment.
- Perform work in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and laws or regulations.

Leadership and People
- Create and foster a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and celebrating differences to ensure a supportive, productive, and fun experience for all team members.
- Perform administrative actions to support team members, including completing payroll, approving vacation and time off requests, approving shift swaps, and other documentation according to policies and procedures.
- Inform people managers of projected team growth needs to support the building of a strong and diverse team based on operational trends and results.
- Establish supportive and productive relationships with all team members, focusing on personal and professional development.

Guest Experience and Community
- Facilitate a seamless end-to-end guest experience by monitoring the incorporation of omnichannel programs (e.g., in-store guest transactions, buy online pickup in store, phone sales, and ship from store).
- Collaborate with team members to ensure an optimal guest experience that values guests’ time and supports store operations.
- Resolve guest feedback and address issues, including guest escalations and urgent requests, helping to “make it right” for guests.

Budget Responsibility
- Accountable for delegated aspects of controllable budget and labor hours

People Management
- Leadership role indirectly responsible for subset of store employees as delegated by Store Manager

What We Look For
- Inclusion & Diversity:  Creates/supports an inclusive environment that values/celebrates differences
- Integrity:  Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner
- Adaptability/Agility: Navigates uncertainty and ambiguity and can change priorities in a fast-paced environment; recovers quickly from setbacks
- Leadership:  Is able and desires to lead and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work
- Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve common goals; seeks connections, partnerships, and diverse perspectives
- Decision Making/Problem Solving: Identifies opportunities for improvement; evaluates alternatives and makes effective, timely decisions
- Strategic Thinking:  Considers the lasting implications of decisions; sets a plan and makes decisions aligned with company strategy, vision, and values
- Business Acumen: Is able to quickly understand and address business information (e.g., profit and loss statements, budgets and sales forecasts, retail strategy and approaches)
- Interactive Communication:  Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others

Job Requirements

Eligibility
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located
- Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods

Schedule/Availability
- Work occurs on a variable schedule which could include early mornings, mornings, afternoons, evenings, late nights or overnights as well as weekends and holidays

Experience
- 1 year experience managing business operations and administration, including experience with scheduling and management of designated labor hours and managing projects or processes

Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)
- Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
- Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
- Experience: 1 year retail or sales specific management experience

Work Context (e.g., environment, interactions, physical)
- Work occurs in an environment with bright lights and loud music
- Work is accomplished as part of a team and also independently
- Work may involve managing conflict or mediating problems between others or deescalating guest issues
- Work involves reaching out to meet and build relationships with strangers/new people, and to strengthen existing community partnerships
- Work is sometimes conducted on a computer or other technical devices, including to meet with others virtually
- Work involves moving through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work, but can also involve sitting for extended periods of time (i.e., more than 1 hour)
- Work may occasionally involve moving boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg)

Compensation & Benefits Package

Base Pay Range : $26.50 - $36.00/hour, subject to minimum wage in the location
Target Bonus: 25%
Total Target Base Pay Range : $33.13 - $45.00/hour

lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our offerings, employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive bonus program and equity offerings, subject to program eligibility requirements.

At lululemon, investing in our people is a top priority. We believe that when life works, work works. We strive to be the place where inclusive leaders come to develop and enable all to be well. Recognizing our teams for their performance and dedication, other components of our total rewards offerings include support of career development, wellbeing, and personal growth:

- Extended health and dental benefits, and mental health plans
- Paid time off
- Savings and retirement plan matching
- Generous employee discount
- Fitness & yoga classes
- Parenthood top-up
- Extensive catalog of development course offerings
- People networks, mentorship programs, and leadership series (to name a few)

Qui nous sommes

lululemon est une entreprise innovante de vêtements performants pour le yoga, la course à pied, l’entraînement et d’autres activités sportives. En établissant des standards élevés en matière de tissus techniques et de design fonctionnel, nous créons des produits et des expériences qui aident les gens à bouger, à croître, à tisser des liens et à se sentir bien. En tant qu’entreprise, nous nous efforçons de créer un changement positif pour construire un avenir sain et prospère. jobs.description:
who we are
lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

about this team
The Global Procurement team are trusted business advisors who strategically partner with internal stakeholders and external suppliers to create value and mitigate risk in strategic non-product purchases for the global organization.  The team supports the business in increasing its profitability and return on investment by creating value in our indirect supply chain through strategic & stakeholder-centric procurement.  From providing category expertise, market insights, cost savings opportunities, supplier performance and relationship management & developing short and long-term strategies, the Global Procurement team plays a key role in value delivery for our business.

About this team

Global Supply Chain Technology delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s supply chain—from raw material innovation and development, costing, sourcing, quality, sustainability and traceability, trade, logistics, and distribution technology. Our team works in close partnership with core business units to ensure that our supply chain remains agile, efficient, and responsive to ever-evolving market demands. By continuously innovating and refining our technological solutions, we enable best-in-class supply chain operations to service our Guests and our stores. This collaborative approach ensures we provide exceptional experiences and support lululemon’s growth in every community we serve.

The role

We are seeking a Technology Director to define and execute the multi year strategy for modernizing and transforming lululemon’s global sourcing technology ecosystem. This leader will shape the strategic roadmap, elevate costing and sourcing platform capabilities, advance AI driven decisioning, and ensure operational excellence across the systems that connect lululemon to its global vendor base.

You will own all aspects of technology for Global Sourcing—architecture, engineering, security, QA automation, operations, and delivery—and oversee a globally distributed team across North America and India. You will be accountable for the platforms that support approximately 300 raw material (RM) and finished goods (FG) vendors globally, and will partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on the technology evolution required to support enterprise initiatives. This role requires a seasoned leader with a proven record of developing a strong leadership bench, managing complex solutions, and thriving in complex, fast paced, and highly collaborative environments.

This role oversees technology solutions supporting:

- Product costing and should-cost modelling (materials, labor, overhead, landed cost)
- Sourcing execution (quoting and RFQ, vendor award, capacity allocation and booking)
- Purchase order management and order lifecycle for raw material and finished goods
- Supplier collaboration portals and vendor-facing self-service
- Partner connectivity (vendors, mills, agents, service providers)
- Integration frameworks (EDI, APIs, event-driven architecture)
- Master data and data quality for cost
- Sourcing analytics, margin visibility, exception management, and operational dashboards

Key responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Roadmap

- Define and deliver a multi year global sourcing technology strategy that enhances scalability, reliability, and speed to market.
- Translate business needs into an actionable engineering roadmap incorporating modernization, cloud migration, supplier collaboration, and responsible AI adoption.
- Partner with business Directors, Sr. Directors, and VPs across Global Sourcing and Costing to define, deliver, and support the strategic roadmap.
- Enroll cross functional technology partners in the strategic vision for Global Sourcing, and lead the creation and expansion of new capabilities that align with our strategic goals.

Platform & Architecture Modernization

- Modernize existing costing and sourcing platforms and integrate next generation capabilities (costing engines, sourcing execution suites, or equivalent).
- Drive transformation toward API-first, event-driven, and scalable integration architectures across the global vendor base.
- Lead design and implementation of secure, resilient, and responsible data management and governance frameworks for material, vendor, and cost master data.
- Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on technology evolution that supports enterprise initiatives.

Engineering Leadership

- Lead globally distributed engineering, QA automation, delivery, and support teams; develop managers and future-ready technical leaders.
- Serve as the escalation point for Technology Managers to support delivery, making thoughtful decisions on the fly and constantly clearing roadblocks.
- Raise engineering standards around quality, observability, security, and system reliability.
- Build high performing, diverse teams with a culture of inclusion, transparency, and continuous improvement, and support career progression and stretch opportunities across the Global Sourcing technology area.

Operational Excellence

- Oversee delivery, operations, and vendor/partner management across sourcing and costing systems, and own the relationship with key vendor partners.
- Manage budgets for strategic initiatives and baseline opex for Global Sourcing technology, ensuring clear ROI and optimization of total cost of ownership.
- Drive root cause analysis, systems reliability, service maturity, and measurable operational improvements.

Innovation & AI Enablement

- Introduce AI-driven decision support for should-cost modelling, quote analysis, capacity allocation, vendor performance, and exception management.
- Champion ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI in sourcing and vendor-facing operations.

Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, related field, or commensurate relative experience.
- 15+ years of experience in technology, including 4+ years in a senior leadership position such as a Technology Manager or Technology Director.
- Experience leading large scale initiatives and modernization efforts for supply chain platforms, with highly valued experience in costing and sourcing areas.
- Proven success delivering transformations in areas such as product costing, sourcing execution, purchase order management, supplier collaboration, or vendor connectivity.
- Strong background in integration architectures (API platforms, EDI, message streaming, event-driven design).
- Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
- Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or Java and familiarity with data engineering patterns.
- Demonstrated ability to manage large budgets and deliver high-impact technology programs.
- Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive influencing skills.
- Continuous learning mindset that stays on the leading edge of sourcing and supply chain technology solutions that can bring value to the organization.
- Experience with AI/ML use cases in supply chain, sourcing, or costing.
- Understanding of apparel or consumer goods product development, raw materials, and global vendor management processes.
- Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones and a global vendor base.

Success metrics:

- Improved cost accuracy, margin visibility, and speed of costing cycles.
- Reduced sourcing and purchase order cycle times, with fewer manual touches per order.
- Improved reliability, uptime, and SLA performance of sourcing and costing systems.
- Strong engagement scores and leadership development of global teams.

jobs.description:
Technology Director | Global Sourcing Technology

Who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About this team

Global Supply Chain Technology delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s supply chain—from raw material innovation and development, costing, sourcing, quality, sustainability and traceability, trade, logistics, and distribution technology. Our team works in close partnership with core business units to ensure that our supply chain remains agile, efficient, and responsive to ever-evolving market demands. By continuously innovating and refining our technological solutions, we enable best-in-class supply chain operations to service our Guests and our stores. This collaborative approach ensures we provide exceptional experiences and support lululemon’s growth in every community we serve.

The role

We are seeking a Technology Director to define and execute the multi year strategy for modernizing and transforming lululemon’s global sourcing technology ecosystem. This leader will shape the strategic roadmap, elevate costing and sourcing platform capabilities, advance AI driven decisioning, and ensure operational excellence across the systems that connect lululemon to its global vendor base.

You will own all aspects of technology for Global Sourcing—architecture, engineering, security, QA automation, operations, and delivery—and oversee a globally distributed team across North America and India. You will be accountable for the platforms that support approximately 300 raw material (RM) and finished goods (FG) vendors globally, and will partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on the technology evolution required to support enterprise initiatives. This role requires a seasoned leader with a proven record of developing a strong leadership bench, managing complex solutions, and thriving in complex, fast paced, and highly collaborative environments.

This role oversees technology solutions supporting:

- Product costing and should-cost modelling (materials, labor, overhead, landed cost)
- Sourcing execution (quoting and RFQ, vendor award, capacity allocation and booking)
- Purchase order management and order lifecycle for raw material and finished goods
- Supplier collaboration portals and vendor-facing self-service
- Partner connectivity (vendors, mills, agents, service providers)
- Integration frameworks (EDI, APIs, event-driven architecture)
- Master data and data quality for cost
- Sourcing analytics, margin visibility, exception management, and operational dashboards

Key responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Roadmap

- Define and deliver a multi year global sourcing technology strategy that enhances scalability, reliability, and speed to market.
- Translate business needs into an actionable engineering roadmap incorporating modernization, cloud migration, supplier collaboration, and responsible AI adoption.
- Partner with business Directors, Sr. Directors, and VPs across Global Sourcing and Costing to define, deliver, and support the strategic roadmap.
- Enroll cross functional technology partners in the strategic vision for Global Sourcing, and lead the creation and expansion of new capabilities that align with our strategic goals.

Platform & Architecture Modernization

- Modernize existing costing and sourcing platforms and integrate next generation capabilities (costing engines, sourcing execution suites, or equivalent).
- Drive transformation toward API-first, event-driven, and scalable integration architectures across the global vendor base.
- Lead design and implementation of secure, resilient, and responsible data management and governance frameworks for material, vendor, and cost master data.
- Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on technology evolution that supports enterprise initiatives.

Engineering Leadership

- Lead globally distributed engineering, QA automation, delivery, and support teams; develop managers and future-ready technical leaders.
- Serve as the escalation point for Technology Managers to support delivery, making thoughtful decisions on the fly and constantly clearing roadblocks.
- Raise engineering standards around quality, observability, security, and system reliability.
- Build high performing, diverse teams with a culture of inclusion, transparency, and continuous improvement, and support career progression and stretch opportunities across the Global Sourcing technology area.

Operational Excellence

- Oversee delivery, operations, and vendor/partner management across sourcing and costing systems, and own the relationship with key vendor partners.
- Manage budgets for strategic initiatives and baseline opex for Global Sourcing technology, ensuring clear ROI and optimization of total cost of ownership.
- Drive root cause analysis, systems reliability, service maturity, and measurable operational improvements.

Innovation & AI Enablement

- Introduce AI-driven decision support for should-cost modelling, quote analysis, capacity allocation, vendor performance, and exception management.
- Champion ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI in sourcing and vendor-facing operations.

Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, related field, or commensurate relative experience.
- 15+ years of experience in technology, including 4+ years in a senior leadership position such as a Technology Manager or Technology Director.
- Experience leading large scale initiatives and modernization efforts for supply chain platforms, with highly valued experience in costing and sourcing areas.
- Proven success delivering transformations in areas such as product costing, sourcing execution, purchase order management, supplier collaboration, or vendor connectivity.
- Strong background in integration architectures (API platforms, EDI, message streaming, event-driven design).
- Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
- Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or Java and familiarity with data engineering patterns.
- Demonstrated ability to manage large budgets and deliver high-impact technology programs.
- Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive influencing skills.
- Continuous learning mindset that stays on the leading edge of sourcing and supply chain technology solutions that can bring value to the organization.
- Experience with AI/ML use cases in supply chain, sourcing, or costing.
- Understanding of apparel or consumer goods product development, raw materials, and global vendor management processes.
- Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones and a global vendor base.

Success metrics:

- Improved cost accuracy, margin visibility, and speed of costing cycles.
- Reduced sourcing and purchase order cycle times, with fewer manual touches per order.
- Improved reliability, uptime, and SLA performance of sourcing and costing systems.
- Strong engagement scores and leadership development of global teams.

Must haves:

In addition to supporting and overseeing export-import operations, the team collaborates closely with our global fulfillment partners as well as within the broader organization to proactively identify and mitigate trade risks. - Monitors and ensures cargo clearance will be completed within agreed KPI.
- Prepares shipping invoices for inbound, outbound & pullback shipments.

- Develops and maintains trade operations policies, procedures, SOPs, best practices and broker audit programs across the APAC region.
- Develops robust metrics to analyze and monitor import compliance and spending; formalizes and executes broker entry audit plan and recordkeeping regime.
- Addresses and escalates customs/trade-related inquiries from internal and external stakeholders. Partners with cross-functional teams (such as distribution, logistics, production, retail operations, etc.) and provides trade operations leadership, guidance and training as necessary.
- Works closely with regional and global trade compliance teams on compliance risks, global initiatives and broader supply chain strategy.
- Supports the launch and ongoing maintenance of trade management platforms across APAC markets.

Who We Are

As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

Job Summary

The Assistant Manager, Operations role is an essential part of the store leadership team and is responsible for making sure our retail business runs smoothly and successfully. Assistant Managers, Operations manage business enablers (including financial, profit and loss [P&L], budget, expenses, and cash) and ensure inventory, supplies, vendor relationships, technology, and facilities are maintained and maximized. They are responsible for writing the store’s weekly schedule and accomplishing people-related administrative activities (including completing payroll and other documentation). Assistant Managers, Operations also execute company-driven operations-focused projects and initiatives at the store level.

Core Responsibilities of the Job

Operations, Product, and Strategy
- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations vision for the store and cascade to team members.
- Plan and prepare weekly team member schedule according to labor requirements, availability, and budget considerations.
- Move dynamically on the retail floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team, and guests.
- Review, monitor, and partner with Store Manager to manage the budget and other business data and metrics (e.g., P&L statement, expenses) and inform planning processes (e.g., quarterly business review and sales planning).
- Provide retail floor leadership to team members, including planning retail floor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of retail floor operations.
- Support sell-through management by ensuring accuracy of inventory counts and coordinating labor hours to efficiently receive product deliveries.
- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives (e.g., from the SSC).
- Understand and adhere to people safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe work environment.
- Perform work in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and laws or regulations.

Leadership and People
- Create and foster a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and celebrating differences to ensure a supportive, productive, and fun experience for all team members.
- Perform administrative actions to support team members, including completing payroll, approving vacation and time off requests, approving shift swaps, and other documentation according to policies and procedures.
- Inform people managers of projected team growth needs to support the building of a strong and diverse team based on operational trends and results.
- Establish supportive and productive relationships with all team members, focusing on personal and professional development.

Guest Experience and Community
- Facilitate a seamless end-to-end guest experience by monitoring the incorporation of omnichannel programs (e.g., in-store guest transactions, buy online pickup in store, phone sales, and ship from store).

- Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve common goals; seeks connections, partnerships, and diverse perspectives
- Decision Making/Problem Solving: Identifies opportunities for improvement; evaluates alternatives and makes effective, timely decisions
- Strategic Thinking:  Considers the lasting implications of decisions; sets a plan and makes decisions aligned with company strategy, vision, and values
- Business Acumen: Is able to quickly understand and address business information (e.g., profit and loss statements, budgets and sales forecasts, retail strategy and approaches)
- Interactive Communication:  Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others

Schedule/Availability

Experience

- Work is accomplished as part of a team and also independently

- Work involves reaching out to meet and build relationships with strangers/new people, and to strengthen existing community partnerships
- Work is sometimes conducted on a computer or other technical devices, including to meet with others virtually
- Work involves moving through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work, but can also involve sitting for extended periods of time (i.e., more than 1 hour)

jobs.description:
Who We Are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

Job Summary

The Assistant Manager, Operations role is an essential part of the store leadership team and is responsible for making sure our retail business runs smoothly and successfully. Assistant Managers, Operations manage business enablers (including financial, profit and loss [P&L], budget, expenses, and cash) and ensure inventory, supplies, vendor relationships, technology, and facilities are maintained and maximized. They are responsible for writing the store’s weekly schedule and accomplishing people-related administrative activities (including completing payroll and other documentation). Assistant Managers, Operations also execute company-driven operations-focused projects and initiatives at the store level.

Core Responsibilities of the Job

Operations, Product, and Strategy
- Implement the Store Manager’s Operations vision for the store and cascade to team members.
- Plan and prepare weekly team member schedule according to labor requirements, availability, and budget considerations.
- Move dynamically on the retail floor to assess and fulfill the needs of the business, team, and guests.
- Review, monitor, and partner with Store Manager to manage the budget and other business data and metrics (e.g., P&L statement, expenses) and inform planning processes (e.g., quarterly business review and sales planning).
- Provide retail floor leadership to team members, including planning retail floor coverage and making decisions to maintain efficiency and effectiveness of retail floor operations.
- Support sell-through management by ensuring accuracy of inventory counts and coordinating labor hours to efficiently receive product deliveries.
- Execute company-level operations-focused directives, projects, and initiatives (e.g., from the SSC).
- Understand and adhere to people safety policies and procedures to maintain a safe work environment.
- Perform work in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and laws or regulations.

Leadership and People
- Create and foster a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and celebrating differences to ensure a supportive, productive, and fun experience for all team members.
- Perform administrative actions to support team members, including completing payroll, approving vacation and time off requests, approving shift swaps, and other documentation according to policies and procedures.
- Inform people managers of projected team growth needs to support the building of a strong and diverse team based on operational trends and results.
- Establish supportive and productive relationships with all team members, focusing on personal and professional development.

Guest Experience and Community
- Facilitate a seamless end-to-end guest experience by monitoring the incorporation of omnichannel programs (e.g., in-store guest transactions, buy online pickup in store, phone sales, and ship from store).
- Collaborate with team members to ensure an optimal guest experience that values guests’ time and supports store operations.
- Resolve guest feedback and address issues, including guest escalations and urgent requests, helping to “make it right” for guests.

Budget Responsibility
- Accountable for delegated aspects of controllable budget and labor hours

People Management
- Leadership role indirectly responsible for subset of store employees as delegated by Store Manager

What We Look For
- Inclusion & Diversity:  Creates/supports an inclusive environment that values/celebrates differences
- Integrity: Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner
- Adaptability/Agility: Navigates uncertainty and ambiguity and can change priorities in a fast-paced environment; recovers quickly from setbacks
- Leadership: Is able and desires to lead and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work
- Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve common goals; seeks connections, partnerships, and diverse perspectives
- Decision Making/Problem Solving: Identifies opportunities for improvement; evaluates alternatives and makes effective, timely decisions
- Strategic Thinking:  Considers the lasting implications of decisions; sets a plan and makes decisions aligned with company strategy, vision, and values
- Business Acumen: Is able to quickly understand and address business information (e.g., profit and loss statements, budgets and sales forecasts, retail strategy and approaches)
- Interactive Communication:  Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others

Job Requirements

Eligibility
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located
- Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods

Schedule/Availability
- Work occurs on a variable schedule which could include early mornings, mornings, afternoons, evenings, late nights or overnights as well as weekends and holidays

Experience
- 1 year experience managing business operations and administration, including experience with scheduling and management of designated labor hours and managing projects or processes

Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)
- Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
- Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
- Experience: 1 year retail or sales specific management experience

Work Context (e.g., environment, interactions, physical)
- Work occurs in an environment with bright lights and loud music
- Work is accomplished as part of a team and also independently
- Work may involve managing conflict or mediating problems between others or deescalating guest issues
- Work involves reaching out to meet and build relationships with strangers/new people, and to strengthen existing community partnerships
- Work is sometimes conducted on a computer or other technical devices, including to meet with others virtually
- Work involves moving through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work, but can also involve sitting for extended periods of time (i.e., more than 1 hour)
- Work may occasionally involve moving boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg)

Compensation & Benefits Package
Base Pay Range : $24.50 - $33.25/hour, subject to minimum wage in the location
Target Bonus: 25%
Total Target Base Pay Range : $30.63 - $41.56/hour

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain Environment
jobs.description:
who we are
lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

about this team
This role is part of the enterprise-wide sustainability team shaping the future of impact within our brand and business. The Director, Supply Chain Environment will be based in our APAC region and be responsible for driving achievement of our Impact Agenda by leading the company’s environmental sustainability strategy and execution across lululemon’s manufacturing supply chain. This role will lead lululemon’s supply chain programs for climate, waste management, and water stewardship across our network of finished goods suppliers and mills. The candidate will drive measurable environmental performance improvements, support environmental compliance, and partner with suppliers, industry organizations, and NGOs. This role requires deep internal partnership with sustainability, sourcing, production, legal, and product quality.

core responsibilities
- Lead lululemon’s environmental sustainability strategy and multi year roadmap across all manufacturing partners, with particular attention on Asia
- Lead implementation of supply chain decarbonization programs to meet our local coal phase out and renewable electricity goals to drive Scope 3 emissions reduction through vendor programs including renewable electricity, thermal decarbonization, energy efficiency and vendor target setting
- Lead water initiatives focused on high risk manufacturing locations. Establish scalable approaches to developing facility-level targets, roadmaps and monitoring execution to meet enterprise goals
- Establish vendor performance expectations and consistently measure progress against those expectations; ensure priorities are integrated into broader sourcing and supply chain strategy
- Partner with RSC operations team to improve quality and usability of supplier environmental data and create performance insights that support decision-making
- Partner with industry stakeholders to define multi-brand solutions to industry problems
- Represent in regional industry collaborations including aii, ACEC, and Cascale
- Serve as the senior regional environmental expert integrating environmental sustainability into sourcing and production teams
- Lead a team of 8-10 environmental and supply chain experts

q ualifications
- 15 years experience working in apparel or footwear supply chains
- 10 years experience implementing environmental or product sustainability programs related to climate and/or water
- Direct experience working with suppliers on environmental programs, preferably apparel or footwear
- Proven ability to excel in a highly collaborative environment with a passion for cross-functional engagement, enrollment and alignment
- Clear communication skills and ability to build relationships with external groups in the supply chain and across the industry
- 5 years experience building and managing a team
- Demonstrated capacity to manage ambiguity, manage multiple priorities, work in a high pressure environment, and manage high profile projects
- Highly strategic thinker with a bias for action
- Strong ability to engage and partner with a variety of stakeholders
- Strong executive presence and ability to simplify complexity into clear, crisp messages and takeaways

must haves
- Acknowledges the presence of choice in every moment and takes personal responsibility for their life.
- Possesses an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovates to achieve great results.
- Communicates with honesty and kindness, and creates the space for others to do the same.
- Leads with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
- Fosters connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
- Integrates fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take themselves too seriously.

additional notes
Immigration support is potentially available for this role.

At lululemon, we care for and invest in the whole person – body, mind, spirit. Our total rewards program is designed to support you in achieving your goals and focus on the things you love. In addition to competitive base pay and a team-based bonus program, we also offer paid time off, generous employee discounts, fitness/yoga classes, parenthood top up program and personal and professional development programs.

work arrangement
